title: Fishcakes
subtitle: Crispy salmon and potato fishcakes
excerpt: Flaked salmon mixed with mashed potato, spring onion, and dill, shaped into patties and pan-fried until golden and crisp. Serve with tartare sauce or a dressed salad.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fishcakes are a traditional British way to extend expensive fish with inexpensive potato, and appear in British cooking at least since the 19th century. The classic version uses smoked haddock or leftover cooked fish mixed with mashed potato, though fresh salmon has become equally popular. The key is to use dry mashed potato and to chill the fishcakes before frying: warm, soft fishcakes will fall apart in the pan.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, heavy pan for even frying.

content.text: The mash must be dry: wet mash produces fishcakes that are too soft to hold their shape. Let the potato steam dry in the pan before mashing. Chill the shaped fishcakes for at least 30 minutes before frying: this firms them up and prevents them breaking apart. Coat lightly in flour just before frying.
Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until tender. Drain and return to the pan over low heat for 1 minute to dry out. Mash until smooth. Leave to cool.
Poach the salmon in simmering water for 8 minutes until just cooked through. Drain and leave to cool. Remove the skin and any bones. Flake into large pieces.
Mix the mash, flaked salmon, spring onion, dill, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt, and pepper together gently. Shape into 8 patties. Dust lightly with flour. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the fishcakes in two batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden. Serve with tartare sauce and a dressed green salad.
